body.zh: 本文已根据 Science X 的编辑流程和政策进行审阅。编辑在确保内容可信度的同时强调了以下属性： 人工智能正在迅速成为人们学习、解决问题和构建知识方式的一部分。然而，人工智能是否会增强人类智力或鼓励过度依赖仍然是一个悬而未决的问题。 北京大学汇丰商学院副教授叶伟明和亚利桑那州立大学沃尔特·克朗凯特新闻与大众传播学院副教授李谦领导的研究小组研究了公众如何讨论人工智能辅助学习。 他们的研究发表在 Comunicar 上，分析了使用人工智能获取、理解和应用知识的认知、行为和道德后果。 人工智能改善了信息的获取并帮助用户高效地完成复杂的任务。但对内容不准确、独立思考能力弱化、抄袭、责任不明确等问题的担忧也与日俱增。因此，研究人员从认知、行为和伦理三个维度以及知识建构的三个阶段——获取、理解和应用来审视人工智能辅助学习。 该研究分析了 2013 年至 2025 年的 Reddit 讨论。在收集的 20,174 条文本中，清理后保留了 10,503 条有效帖子。研究人员利用 Biterm 主题模型 (BTM) 和定性分析，确定了公众对人工智能如何改变学习和知识构建的主要担忧。 在知识获取过程中，用户赞赏人工智能的速度和组织信息的能力，但事实错误和有缺陷的推理造成了“可信度焦虑”。在知识理解过程中，人工智能让困难的概念更容易掌握，而过度依赖则可能会削弱独立推理和批判性思维。一些用户的反应是限制人工智能的使用并自行重建知识。 在知识应用过程中，人工智能降低了试错成本，并提供了新的解决问题路径。然而，它也引发了对抄袭、知识产权、公平和责任的担忧。总体而言，公众态度遵循信任、怀疑和重新调整的循环。人工智能的使用也从个人实验扩展到结果比较、协作验证和社区检查。 研究表明，人工智能正日益成为智力合作伙伴、行为促进者和道德对话者，而不仅仅是一种工具。 研究人员认为，人工智能辅助学习是一场关于效率、信任、自主和责任的持续谈判。他们呼吁透明、参与性和分阶段的治理，可以与人工智能技术一起发展。 WeiMing Ye 等人，“人工智能让我们变得更聪明吗？还是……

reflection.en: The rapid advancement of AI presents a profound question: does it serve as a tool to amplify our God-given intellect, or does it risk diminishing our capacity for independent thought? As knowledge expands at an unprecedented rate, as prophesied in Daniel, we are called to discern how these powerful tools shape our minds and our relationship with truth.
reflection.zh: 人工智能的飞速发展提出了一个深刻的问题：它是否会成为放大我们上帝所赐智慧的工具，还是会削弱我们独立思考的能力？正如但以理书所预言的，随着知识以前所未有的速度增长，我们被呼召去辨别这些强大的工具如何塑造我们的思想以及我们与真理的关系。

verse.textEn: But you, Daniel, roll up and seal the words of the scroll until the time of the end. Many will go here and there to increase knowledge.
verse.textZh: 但以理啊，你要隐藏这话，封闭这书，直到末时。必有多人来往奔跑，知识就必增长。

title.en: The farmer who turned to singing after bovine TB silenced his fields
title.zh: 农民因牛结核病而失业，转而唱歌

summary.en: Dairy farmer Mervyn Kelso experienced profound sadness and emptiness after losing his entire herd to bovine TB. He found solace and a new path through joining a choir, which lifted his spirits and led to unexpected opportunities.
summary.zh: 奶牛养殖户 Mervyn Kelso 在因牛结核病失去整个牛群后，经历了巨大的悲伤和空虚。他通过加入合唱团找到了慰藉和新的生活方向，这提升了他的精神，并带来了意想不到的机会。

body.en:
When bovine TB led to the loss of his entire herd, dairy farmer Mervyn Kelso struggled with the sadness of the empty fields and the silence of the milking yard.

It was a traumatic time for a man who had farmed his whole life, and it was hard watching his neighbours tend to their cows.

His sister suggested he should join the Farmers' Choir and that turned out to be a "great lifter".

Fast forward four years, and Mervyn has sang for the King, met musical royalty and his choir is up for a national award.

Mervyn's first batch of cows were lost in November 2021. At the same time, a friend who had been around the County Antrim farm for three generations died.

Mervyn and his wife Ruth, who live near Portglenone, relied on their faith for "the strength to carry on".

Mervyn would sing in church and so when the Farmers' Choir restarted in nearby Ballymena that autumn, he decided to give it a go.

He said it had been rewarding and different - a relief to the tough challenges of day-to-day farming.

"Farming is one very lonely job, even more lonely than it was a generation ago, because labour is so difficult to get," he said.

"It has the effect of depressing you, and that's why being involved in such a thing as a choir or any social event outside farming is good for anyone."

"It was a hard time for both of us and the choir was definitely a great lifter," she said.

"It was just great to have something to lift us because you weren't busy on the farm - well, you did some extra odd jobs, but it wasn't like the usual level of busyness."

She said she has made "some lovely friends" and they get to see each other at choir rehearsals, concerts and céilís.

"Sometimes you see a different side of a choir member when you're not just sitting beside them singing, and that's really good, socially," she added.

He grew up on a dairy farm and remembers his father talking about people at harvest time, helping each other out then sharing "a bit of craic and banter".

He said the choir helped fill a social gap that has emerged in rural life as farming has become more automated.

"Social isolation and loneliness - the sad thing is in rural communities, people don't always like to talk about that and acknowledge that," he said.

Nine of the friends, including Mervyn and Ruth, found themselves singing in the choir as part of the King's Coronation concert .

They met the Duke and Duchess of Edinburgh, and Mervyn also met one of his heroes - Welsh bass-baritone Bryn Terfel, whose father was a sheep farmer.

"We were running around with these Farmers' Choir vests, and he spotted us and he stopped and talked to us," he said.

"I'm a teacher - teaching can be stressful and farmers have their stresses on the farm, and you can see it on their faces.

"They go into their practice,...
body.zh: 当牛结核病导致整个牛群死亡时，奶农默文·凯尔索 (Mervyn Kelso) 在空荡荡的田野和挤奶场的寂静中与悲伤作斗争。 对于一个一生务农的人来说，这是一段痛苦的时光，看着邻居照顾牛也很难过。 他的姐姐建议他加入农民合唱团，结果证明他是一名“伟大的举重运动员”。 四年过去了，默文为国王演唱，会见了音乐界的皇室成员，他的合唱团即将获得国家奖项。 Mervyn 的第一批奶牛于 2021 年 11 月丢失。与此同时，一位在安特里姆郡农场生活了三代的朋友也去世了。 住在波特格莱诺附近的默文和他的妻子露丝依靠他们的信仰来“继续前进”。 默文会在教堂唱歌，因此当农民合唱团那年秋天在附近的巴利米纳重新开始时，他决定尝试一下。 他说，这是有益且不同的——缓解了日常农业的严峻挑战。 “农业是一项非常孤独的工作，甚至比上一代人更加孤独，因为劳动力很难获得，”他说。 “它会让你感到沮丧，这就是为什么参加合唱团或农业以外的任何社交活动对任何人都有好处。” “这对我们俩来说都是一段艰难的时光，合唱团绝对是一位伟大的举重运动员，”她说。 “能有一些东西来鼓舞我们真是太好了，因为你在农场并不忙——嗯，你做了一些额外的零工，但这并不像平常那​​样忙碌。” 她说她结识了“一些可爱的朋友”，他们可以在合唱团排练、音乐会和聚会上见面。 “有时，当你不只是坐在合唱团成员旁边唱歌时，你会看到他们的不同侧面，这在社交方面真的很好，”她补充道。 他在一个奶牛场长大，记得父亲在收获季节谈论人们，互相帮助，然后分享“一些疯狂和玩笑”。 他说，随着农业变得更加自动化，合唱团帮助填补了农村生活中出现的社会差距。 “社会孤立和孤独——可悲的是在农村社区，人们并不总是喜欢谈论并承认这一点，”他说。 包括默文和露丝在内的九位朋友发现自己在合唱团中唱歌，作为国王加冕音乐会的一部分。 他们遇到了爱丁堡公爵和公爵夫人，默文还遇到了他的英雄之一——威尔士男中音布林·特菲尔，他的父亲是一位牧羊人。 “我们穿着这些农民合唱团的背心跑来跑去，他发现了我们，然后停下来和我们说话，”他说。 “我是一名老师——教学压力很大，农民在农场也有压力，你可以从他们的脸上看到。 “他们开始练习，......

reflection.en: The silence of Mervyn Kelso's fields after losing his herd to bovine TB speaks of deep loss and despair. Yet, when he joined the Farmers' Choir, he found his strength renewed, much like the prophet's promise that those who wait for Yahweh will soar on wings like eagles. His story shows that even in the face of devastating loss, new life and purpose can be...
reflection.zh: Mervyn Kelso 在因牛结核病失去牛群后，田野的寂静诉说着深切的失落和绝望。然而，当他加入农民合唱团时，他找到了力量的更新，这与先知应许那些等候雅伟的人必如鹰展翅上腾的应许相似。他的故事表明，即使面对毁灭性的损失，也能通过意想不到的途径找到新的生命和目标。

verse.textEn: Those who hope in Yahweh will renew their strength. They will soar on wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary.
verse.textZh: 但那等候雅伟的，必从新得力。他们必如鹰展翅上腾。

title.en: New mesothelioma drug turns cancer’s own defenses against it
title.zh: 新型间皮瘤药物利用癌细胞自身的防御机制

summary.en: Scientists are investigating an unconventional approach to treating mesothelioma, a severe cancer linked to asbestos exposure with limited treatment options. A new experimental drug targets mesothelioma by inhibiting PRX3, an antioxidant defense that tumors rely on to withstand significant oxidative stress. Initial...
summary.zh: 科学家们正在探索一种对抗间皮瘤的非常规方法，间皮瘤是一种与石棉暴露相关的、治疗选择有限的严重癌症。一种新的实验性药物通过抑制 PRX3 来靶向间皮瘤，PRX3 是一种肿瘤赖以承受显著氧化应激的抗氧化防御机制。初步的临床试验结果显示，67% 的患者疾病进展得到控制，并且生存率令人鼓舞，这表明该策略未来可能适用于其他癌症。

body.en: Scientists are testing a counterintuitive way to fight mesothelioma, an aggressive asbestos-linked cancer with few effective treatments. A new experimental mesothelioma drug kills cancer cells by disabling PRX3, an antioxidant defense that tumors use to survive intense oxidative stress. In an early clinical trial, it controlled disease progression in 67% of patients and produced encouraging survival results, raising hopes that the strategy could eventually be used against other cancers.
body.zh: 科学家们正在测试一种违反直觉的方法来对抗间皮瘤，这是一种与石棉相关的侵袭性癌症，几乎没有有效的治疗方法。一种新的实验性间皮瘤药物通过禁用 PRX3 来杀死癌细胞，PRX3 是一种抗氧化防御系统，肿瘤用来生存强烈的氧化应激。在一项早期临床试验中，它控制了 67% 患者的疾病进展，并产生了令人鼓舞的生存结果，这让人们希望该策略最终可以用于治疗其他癌症。

reflection.en: The pursuit of healing often involves a deep dive into the intricate workings of the created world. This research into mesothelioma, by understanding and then subverting a tumor's own defenses, reflects a profound engagement with biological complexity. It reminds us that wisdom and solutions can be found by observing and learning from the very systems...
reflection.zh: 治愈的追求常常涉及深入研究被造世界的复杂运作。这项关于间皮瘤的研究，通过理解然后颠覆肿瘤自身的防御机制，体现了对生物复杂性的深刻参与。它提醒我们，智慧和解决方案可以在观察和学习雅伟所设定的系统本身中找到。

verse.textEn: But ask the animals, and they will teach you, or the birds in the sky, and they will tell you; or speak to the earth, and it will teach you, or let the fish in the sea inform you.
verse.textZh: 你且问走兽，走兽必指教你；又问空中的飞鸟，飞鸟必告诉你。或与地说话，地必指教你；海中的鱼也必向你说明。

title.en: Rare tree offspring given lifeline at Scottish botanic garden
title.zh: 苏格兰植物园为稀有树木后代提供生命线

summary.en: Logan Botanic Garden is assisting in the preservation of a tree species indigenous to Robinson Crusoe Island in the South Pacific. Conservationists are intensifying efforts to prevent the species from becoming extinct by establishing a new home for two seedlings from the last known wild dendroseris neriifolia tree,...
summary.zh: 洛根植物园正在协助保护一种原产于南太平洋鲁滨逊漂流者岛的树木。保护主义者正通过为世界上仅存的一棵野生 dendroseris neriifolia 树的两个幼苗建立新家，来加紧努力防止该物种灭绝，这棵树目前仅作为单一植株悬挂在悬崖上。

body.en:
The offspring of one of the world's rarest trees has been given a new home in south-west Scotland as conservationists step up efforts to save the species from extinction.

Two seedlings from the last known wild dendroseris neriifolia tree have arrived at Logan Botanic Garden in Dumfries and Galloway after an international rescue effort involving experts in Chile and the UK.

The species, native to Robinson Crusoe Island in the South Pacific, has been pushed to the brink by habitat loss, invasive species and repeated wildfires.

Conservationists hope the move will provide a vital safeguard for the future of a plant that now survives in the wild as a single tree clinging to a cliff face.

The dendroseris neriifolia, a rare tree daisy found only on Chile's Robinson Crusoe Island, has suffered a dramatic decline over recent decades.

By 1980, only eight wild specimens remained, and although reintroduction projects were launched in the early 2000s, the breakdown of protection measures in 2017 left the species vulnerable once again to invasive plants and grazing animals.

Today, the last surviving wild tree is supported by ropes on a steep volcanic outcrop to prevent it from falling.

In May this year, 29 seeds were collected from the lone tree and sent to the Millennium Seed Bank at Kew Wakehurst.

Eight seedlings successfully germinated, with two now transferred to Logan Botanic Garden, where the climate is considered particularly suitable for rare Chilean plants. The remaining seedlings will stay at Kew.

Richard Baines, curator at Logan, described the arrival as a significant moment and said the garden could play an important role in learning more about the species and helping secure its future.

"Experience shows that plant species from the Juan Fernández Islands do well at Logan," he said.

"Creating a safe place for these seedlings, getting to know them, and learning more about their adaption to different environments, gives us the chance to contribute so much more."

Scientists involved in the project said the international collaboration offered a rare opportunity to prevent the extinction of a unique plant lineage and preserve part of the natural heritage of the Juan Fernández archipelago.

Diego Penneckamp, a scientist at Jardín Botánico VerdeNativo, said saving the species was a "race against time".

"This international collaboration to support the last remaining individual could prevent the extinction of a species that represents a unique lineage with its own natural history," he said.
body.zh: 随着自然资源保护主义者加紧努力拯救该物种免遭灭绝，世界上最稀有的树木之一的后代在苏格兰西南部找到了新家。 经过智利和英国专家参与的国际救援努力，最后一棵已知的野生树突树的两棵幼苗已抵达邓弗里斯和加洛韦的洛根植物园。 该物种原产于南太平洋的鲁宾逊克鲁索岛，由于栖息地丧失、入侵物种和反复发生的野火，已被推向边缘。 环保主义者希望此举能为这种植物的未来提供重要的保障，这种植物目前在野外以单棵树的形式生存在悬崖表面。 树突花是一种仅在智利鲁宾逊克鲁索岛上发现的稀有雏菊，近几十年来其数量急剧减少。 到 1980 年，只剩下 8 个野生标本，尽管在 2000 年代初启动了重新引入项目，但 2017 年保护措施的崩溃使该物种再次容易受到入侵植物和食草动物的侵害。 如今，最后一棵幸存的野生树被绳索支撑在陡峭的火山露头上，以防止其倒下。 今年 5 月，人们从这棵孤树上收集了 29 粒种子，并送往位于 Kew Wakehurst 的千年种子库。 八棵幼苗成功发芽，其中两棵现已转移到洛根植物园，那里的气候被认为特别适合稀有的智利植物。剩下的幼苗将留在邱园。 洛根博物馆馆长理查德·贝恩斯 (Richard Baines) 将此次到来描述为一个重要时刻，并表示该花园可以在更多地了解该物种并帮助确保其未来方面发挥重要作用。 “经验表明，来自胡安·费尔南德斯群岛的植物物种在洛根生长得很好，”他说。 “为这些幼苗创造一个安全的地方，了解它们，并更多地了解它们对不同环境的适应，使我们有机会做出更多贡献。” 参与该项目的科学家表示，国际合作提供了一个难得的机会，可以防止独特的植物谱系灭绝，并保护胡安·费尔南德斯群岛的部分自然遗产。 Jardín Botánico VerdeNativo 的科学家迭戈·彭内坎普 (Diego Penneckamp) 表示，拯救该物种是“与时间赛跑”。 他说：“这种支持最后一个个体的国际合作可以防止一个代表着具有自己的自然历史的独特谱系的物种的灭绝。”

reflection.en: In the face of extinction, conservationists have intervened to protect the rare dendroseris neriifolia tree, giving its young a chance to thrive. This act of stewardship mirrors the biblical mandate to care for the earth and its inhabitants, recognizing the intrinsic value of every living thing.
reflection.zh: 面对灭绝的威胁，保护主义者介入保护稀有的 dendroseris neriifolia 树，让它们的后代有机会茁壮成长。这种管理行为呼应了圣经中照顾大地及其居民的使命，认识到每一种生物的内在价值。

verse.textEn: Yahweh God took the man and put him in the Garden of Eden to work it and take care of it.
verse.textZh: 雅伟神将那人安置在伊甸园，使他修理看守。

title.en: NASA’s New Horizons spots signs of liquid nitrogen flowing on Pluto
title.zh: 新视野号探测器发现冥王星上有液氮流动的迹象

summary.en: Scientists have discovered the first evidence suggesting that liquid may have flowed across Pluto's surface recently. Dark markings on the large Sputnik Planitia glacier are consistent with liquid nitrogen rising through cracks from deep below the ice, indicating Pluto might be more geologically active than its icy...
summary.zh: 科学家们发现了第一个证据，表明液态物质可能在近期流过冥王星的表面。巨大的斯普特尼克平原冰川上的深色特征与液氮从冰层深处通过裂缝上升的现象一致，这表明冥王星的地理活动可能比其冰冻的外表所显示的更为活跃。

body.en: Scientists have found the first evidence that liquid may have flowed across Pluto’s surface in the recent past. Dark features on the enormous Sputnik Planitia glacier appear consistent with liquid nitrogen rising through cracks from deep beneath the ice. Computer models show that nitrogen could melt at the glacier’s base and travel upward like fluid through small conduits. The finding reveals that Pluto may be much more geologically active than its frozen appearance suggests.
body.zh: 科学家们发现了第一个证据，表明液体在不久前可能流过冥王星表面。巨大的斯普特尼克平原冰川上的黑色特征似乎与从冰层深处的裂缝中升起的液氮一致。计算机模型显示，氮气可以在冰川底部融化，并像液体一样通过小管道向上流动。这一发现表明，冥王星的地质活动可能比其冰冻外观所暗示的要活跃得多。

reflection.en: The New Horizons mission's findings on Pluto challenge our assumptions about frozen worlds. The possibility of liquid nitrogen flowing beneath Sputnik Planitia reminds us that creation holds profound complexities and activity, often hidden from immediate view. As Job asks, 'But ask the animals, and they will teach you, or the birds of the sky, and they will...
reflection.zh: “新视野号”探测器在冥王星上的发现挑战了我们对冰冻世界的固有看法。斯普特尼克平原冰川下可能存在液氮流动的可能性，提醒我们造物充满了深刻的复杂性和活动性，这些往往隐藏在不易察觉之处。正如约伯所问：“但你且问走兽，可也教导你；空中的飞鸟，也可告诉你；或与地说话，地必指教你；海中的鱼，也必向你说明。”（约伯记 12:7-8）。

verse.textEn: But ask the animals, and they will teach you, or the birds in the sky, and they will tell you; or speak to the earth, and it will teach you, or let the fish in the sea inform you.
verse.textZh: 你且问走兽，走兽必指教你；又问空中的飞鸟，飞鸟必告诉你。或与地说话，地必指教你；海中的鱼也必向你说明。

title.en: The week that changed maths for ever – podcast
title.zh: 改变数学的‘一周’——播客

summary.en: In early September, OpenAI announced it had solved a major mathematics problem that has stumped humans for nearly a century. The news left mathematicians reeling, and many expressed concern over what will be left for humans as AI becomes ever more adept at unravelling complex problems. Now 25 recipients of the Fields...
summary.zh: 九月初，OpenAI宣布已解决一个困扰人类近百年的重大数学难题。这一消息令数学界震惊，许多人担心随着人工智能在解开复杂问题方面越来越得心应手，人类将何去何从。如今，25位菲尔兹奖（常被称为数学界的诺贝尔奖）得主联名发表公开信，表达了对人工智能公司与其领域之间“严重脱节”的担忧。为了解人工智能将如何颠覆数学——以及数学家...

body.en: In early September, OpenAI announced it had solved a major mathematics problem that has stumped humans for nearly a century. The news left mathematicians reeling, and many expressed concern over what will be left for humans as AI becomes ever more adept at unravelling complex problems. Now 25 recipients of the Fields medal – often called the Nobel prize for maths – have signed an open letter expressing their fears of a ‘severe misalignment’ between AI companies and their field. To find out how AI is likely to upend maths – and how mathematicians might respond – Ian Sample speaks to Colva Roney-Dougal, professor of pure mathematics at the University of St Andrews ‘Immature playground boasting’: mathematicians uneasy at OpenAI’s latest scalp Support the Guardian: theguardian.com/sciencepod Continue reading...
body.zh: 9月初，OpenAI宣布解决了困扰人类近一个世纪的重大数学问题。这一消息让数学家感到震惊，许多人对随着人工智能变得越来越擅长解决复杂问题而给人类留下的东西表示担忧。现在，菲尔兹奖（通常被称为数学诺贝尔奖）的 25 名获得者签署了一封公开信，表达了他们对人工智能公司与其领域之间“严重脱节”的担忧。为了了解人工智能可能如何颠覆数学，以及数学家会如何应对，Ian Sample 与圣安德鲁斯大学纯数学教授 Colva Roney-Dougal 进行了对话“不成熟的操场吹嘘”：数学家对 OpenAI 的最新头皮感到不安 支持卫报：theguardian.com/sciencepod 继续阅读...

reflection.en: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence, exemplified by OpenAI solving a century-old math problem, echoes the ancient prophecy that 'knowledge shall increase' in the latter days. This technological leap, while astounding, also raises profound questions about humanity's role and purpose in an increasingly intelligent world. As we witness these...
reflection.zh: 人工智能的飞速发展，例如OpenAI解决了百年数学难题，呼应了古老的预言——在末世“知识必增长”。这项技术飞跃虽然令人惊叹，但也引发了关于人类在日益智能化的世界中的角色和目的的深刻问题。当我们见证这些发展时，我们被呼召寻求智慧和分辨力，确保我们对知识的追求能造福所有人。

verse.textEn: But you, Daniel, roll up and seal the words of the scroll until the time of the end. Many will go here and there to increase knowledge.
verse.textZh: 但以理啊，你要隐藏这话，封闭这书，直到末时。必有多人来往奔跑，知识就必增长。

title.en: What the Bayeux tapestry reveals about medieval buildings on both sides of the Channel
title.zh: 贝叶挂毯揭示海峡两岸的中世纪建筑

summary.en: The Bayeux Tapestry, often remembered for its depictions of ships, horses, and the Battle of Hastings, also contains valuable information for architectural historians. The tapestry illustrates 33 different buildings, ranging from grand palaces and religious structures to ordinary houses, offering insights into...
summary.zh: 贝叶挂毯（Bayeux Tapestry）常让人联想到战船、骏马和黑斯廷斯战役的场景，但它也为建筑史学家提供了宝贵的资料。挂毯描绘了33种不同的建筑，涵盖了宫殿、宗教建筑、普通住宅等，为人们了解11世纪的建筑风格和技术提供了视角。

body.en:
This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:

For many, the Bayeux Tapestry conjures images of clinker-built ships, prancing horses, the Normans feasting on chicken on the eve of the Battle of Hastings, and the arrow in King Harold's eye that ended centuries of Anglo-Saxon rule.

But for the architectural historian, it is the 33 buildings represented on the Bayeux Embroidery that catch the eye. These buildings range from palaces and religious buildings to two-story houses and simple dwellings. They give the beholder some idea of what the 11th-century built environment looked like on either side of the Channel, even though the representations are formulaic, general impressions—as was the normal way to depict buildings in the era.

This suggests that the designer of the tapestry was familiar with the work done in certain monastic scriptoria (writing rooms), each of which had its own distinct style. The same holds true for many of the design elements, such as birds and animals, shown in the borders of the tapestry that reveal parallels with the Romanesque sculpture of Ely cathedral .

This familiarity with the scriptorium and the stonemason's yard implies that the Bayeux Tapestry's designs were created by a trained artist and then used by embroiderers, though what we know about them is pure speculation. Some scholars believe the tapestry may have been created in England by nuns from Barking Abbey in Canterbury, as the skillful needlework bears similarities to other works of English embroidery from the 11th century.

The sequence of scenes starts with Edward the Confessor sending his brother-in-law Harold on a mission to Normandy. The king is enthroned in a large hall with turrets on the corners. To show the interior, the outer wall has been removed. What is more, to the left of the hall, the exterior of the impressive entrance porch is rotated a quarter-turn so the viewer can see it.

To tell the story and indicate a palatial setting, it sufficed to show a grand entrance and great hall. In much the same way, the abbey of Mont-Saint-Michel is shown as a building on top of a rock. Although this typified the monastery's setting, the vignette can in no way be used for reconstructing the 11th-century abbey. The conventions of the time clearly preferred abstraction over naturalism.

Most buildings on the tapestry, as in reality, were made of timber. Stone architecture was still mainly used for ecclesiastical buildings such as Westminster Abbey, by far the largest building shown on the tapestry. Construction began under Edward the Confessor in the grand Norman style and had not yet been completed in early 1066, despite the...
body.zh: 本文已根据 Science X 的编辑流程和政策进行审阅。编辑在确保内容可信度的同时强调了以下属性： 对于许多人来说，贝叶挂毯让人联想到熟料建造的船只、腾跃的马匹、诺曼人在黑斯廷斯战役前夕享用鸡肉，以及哈罗德国王眼中的箭结束了几个世纪的盎格鲁撒克逊统治。 但对于建筑历史学家来说，最吸引眼球的是贝叶刺绣上描绘的 33 座建筑。这些建筑的范围从宫殿、宗教建筑到二层房屋和简易民居。它们让观看者对英吉利海峡两岸 11 世纪的建筑环境有所了解，尽管这些表现是公式化的、一般性的印象——这是描绘那个时代建筑的正常方式。 这表明挂毯的设计者熟悉某些修道院的写字室（写作室）中所做的工作，每个房间都有自己独特的风格。这同样适用于许多设计元素，例如挂毯边框中显示的鸟类和动物，与伊利大教堂的罗马式雕塑有相似之处。 这种对写字间和石匠院子的熟悉意味着贝叶挂毯的设计是由训练有素的艺术家创作的，然后由刺绣师使用，尽管我们对它们的了解纯粹是猜测。一些学者认为，这幅挂毯可能是由坎特伯雷巴金修道院的修女在英国创作的，因为其精湛的针线工艺与 11 世纪其他英国刺绣作品有相似之处。 这一系列场景始于忏悔者爱德华派他的妹夫哈罗德前往诺曼底执行任务。国王在一个大厅里加冕，大厅的角落里有角塔。为了展示内部，外墙已被拆除。更重要的是，在大厅的左侧，令人印象深刻的入口门廊的外部旋转了四分之一圈，以便观众可以看到它。 为了讲述故事并展现富丽堂皇的环境，展示一个宏伟的入口和大厅就足够了。以大致相同的方式，圣米歇尔山修道院被显示为岩石顶部的建筑。尽管这代表了修道院的背景，但该插图绝不能用于重建 11 世纪的修道院。当时的惯例显然更喜欢抽象而不是自然主义。 与现实一样，挂毯上的大多数建筑物都是由木材制成的。石头建筑仍然主要用于教会建筑，例如威斯敏斯特教堂，这是迄今为止挂毯上显示的最大的建筑。在忏悔者爱德华 (Edward the Confessor) 的领导下，这座宏伟的诺曼风格建筑开始兴建，尽管...

reflection.en: The Bayeux Tapestry, a remarkable piece of 11th-century artistry, serves as a historical record, offering glimpses into the built environment of its time. It reminds us that wisdom and understanding can be gleaned from careful observation of human endeavors and the world around us, much like Job's observation that creation itself speaks of its Maker's...
reflection.zh: 贝叶挂 असते，一件非凡的11世纪艺术品，作为历史记录，让我们得以窥见那个时代的建筑环境。它提醒我们，智慧和理解可以从仔细观察人类的努力和周围的世界中获得，正如约伯所观察到的，受造之物本身就诉说着造物主的智慧。...

verse.textEn: But ask the animals, and they will teach you, or the birds in the sky, and they will tell you; or speak to the earth, and it will teach you, or let the fish in the sea inform you.
verse.textZh: 你且问走兽，走兽必指教你；又问空中的飞鸟，飞鸟必告诉你。或与地说话，地必指教你；海中的鱼也必向你说明。

title.en: Hidden “immune organ” in the skull may help fight brain cancer
title.zh: 颅内隐藏的“免疫器官”可能有助于对抗脑癌

summary.en: Scientists have discovered a previously unknown "immune organ" within the skull of mice that functions as a rapid first responder against brain cancer. Enhancing this local immune defense led to improved tumor rejection and survival rates, suggesting potential new treatments targeting the skull's immune system....
summary.zh: 科学家发现小鼠颅骨骨髓中存在先前未知的淋巴结样免疫结构，这些结构能迅速响应脑癌。加强这种局部免疫防御能力可提高肿瘤排斥率和生存率，这为靶向颅骨的免疫系统提供了新的治疗可能性。研究人员在人体颅骨骨髓中也发现了类似的免疫细胞，表明这种局部防御系统可能并非仅限于小鼠。

body.en:
Researchers at Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis have identified previously unknown lymph node-like immune structures in the skull bone marrow of mice. The findings suggest these nearby immune hubs can respond rapidly to brain cancer, becoming active before more distant lymph nodes even receive signals that something is wrong.

The team also found evidence of similar immune cells in human skull bone marrow, suggesting that this local defense system may not be limited to mice.

Scientists once believed that the brain was largely isolated from the immune system. That view has changed dramatically in recent years. The new findings suggest the brain not only communicates with immune cells, but may also have specialized immune "security stations" positioned unusually close by.

Published in Nature , the study is the first to identify immune hubs of this kind inside bone.

"This study reveals that the skull bone marrow is far more than just a structural framework -- it harbors previously unrecognized hubs for brain-specific immune responses," said senior author Jonathan Kipnis, PhD, the Alan A. and Edith L. Wolff Distinguished Professor of Pathology & Immunology and a BJC Investigator at WashU Medicine. "Uncovering this localized immune niche changes how we view neuroimmune interactions and opens exciting new avenues for treating brain tumors and other neurological diseases."

Earlier work from Kipnis' laboratory helped overturn the long-standing idea that the brain was separated from the immune system. The group discovered lymphatic vessels in the dura mater, the protective outer layer of tissue surrounding the brain just beneath the skull.

More recently, the researchers found tiny physical channels bridging the skull, dura, and brain tissue . Those channels provide a direct route through which immune cells and cellular waste can travel between the brain and nearby skull bone marrow.

In the new mouse study, the scientists followed proteins as they moved out of the brain, through these channels, and into the skull bone marrow. There, they discovered organized immune structures resembling those normally found in lymph nodes.

Lymph nodes serve as important coordination centers for immune activity. Within them, T follicular helper cells support B cells, which can then produce large quantities of antibodies that help the body fight infections and disease. Finding comparable structures in healthy bone marrow was unexpected.

"We have never seen such structures in healthy bone marrow before," said Jang Hyun Park, PhD, the study's first author and a postdoctoral research fellow in the Kipnis lab who is starting his own lab at the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology this fall. "It is an exciting discovery that points out that...
body.zh: 圣路易斯华盛顿大学医学院的研究人员在小鼠头骨骨髓中发现了以前未知的淋巴结样免疫结构。研究结果表明，这些附近的免疫中枢可以对脑癌做出快速反应，甚至在更远的淋巴结收到出现问题的信号之前就变得活跃。 研究小组还在人类头骨骨髓中发现了类似免疫细胞的证据，表明这种局部防御系统可能不仅限于小鼠。 科学家曾经认为大脑在很大程度上与免疫系统是隔离的。近年来，这种观点发生了巨大变化。新发现表明，大脑不仅与免疫细胞进行交流，而且可能还具有位于异常接近的位置的专门免疫“安全站”。 该研究发表在《自然》杂志上，是第一个在骨骼内识别出这种免疫中枢的研究。 “这项研究表明，头骨骨髓不仅仅是一个结构框架，它还蕴藏着以前未被认识的大脑特异性免疫反应中枢，”华盛顿大学医学院病理学和免疫学杰出教授、BJC 研究员、资深作者 Jonathan Kipnis 博士说。 “发现这种局部免疫生态位改变了我们看待神经免疫相互作用的方式，并为治疗脑肿瘤和其他神经系统疾病开辟了令人兴奋的新途径。” 基普尼斯实验室的早期工作帮助推翻了长期以来认为大脑与免疫系统分离的观点。研究小组在硬脑膜中发现了淋巴管，硬脑膜是颅骨下方大脑周围的保护性外层组织。 最近，研究人员发现了连接头骨、硬脑膜和脑组织的微小物理通道。这些通道提供了免疫细胞和细胞废物在大脑和附近的颅骨骨髓之间移动的直接途径。 在这项新的小鼠研究中，科学家们追踪了蛋白质从大脑中移出，通过这些通道进入头骨骨髓的过程。在那里，他们发现了类似于淋巴结中常见的有组织的免疫结构。 淋巴结是免疫活动的重要协调中心。其中，滤泡辅助 T 细胞支持 B 细胞，然后 B 细胞可以产生大量抗体，帮助身体抵抗感染和疾病。在健康骨髓中发现类似的结构是出乎意料的。 该研究的第一作者、Kipnis 实验室的博士后研究员 Jang Hyun Park 博士说：“我们以前从未在健康的骨髓中看到过这样的结构。”他将于今年秋天在韩国科学技术院建立自己的实验室。 “这是一个令人兴奋的发现，它指出......

reflection.en: The intricate design of the body, even in unexpected places like skull bone marrow, reveals the profound wisdom embedded in creation. This discovery of a "hidden immune organ" reminds us that Yahweh's handiwork is vast and often surprising, offering new avenues for healing and hope. As we learn more about the body's complex systems, we are invited to marvel...
reflection.zh: 身体的精妙设计，即使在颅骨骨髓这样意想不到的地方，也揭示了创造中蕴含的深刻智慧。这一“隐藏免疫器官”的发现提醒我们，雅伟的作为浩瀚且常出人意料，为治愈和希望带来了新的途径。 当我们更多地了解身体复杂的系统时，我们被邀请惊叹于造物主的智慧，并在理解祂的创造中寻求智慧，正如约伯所观察到的，连走兽飞鸟也能教导我们。

title.en: Why Melbourne makes you sneeze in spring
title.zh: 为什么墨尔本让你在春天打喷嚏

summary.en: Spring in Melbourne brings flowering plants and, consequently, pollen that triggers hay fever and seasonal asthma for approximately one in five residents. Pollen counts are monitored and published daily from October to December to help manage these conditions.
summary.zh: 墨尔本的春天带来了开花的植物，进而导致花粉症和季节性哮喘，影响了约五分之一的居民。从十月到十二月，花粉计数每天都会被监测和发布，以帮助管理这些疾病。

body.en:
This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:

When most Australians say 'spring is in the air,' they're speaking metaphorically, as the days become longer and warmer.

Spring is the time of year when Melbourne's air becomes laden with pollen from plants beginning to flower.

And while those budding blooms bring joy to many people, for about one in five Melburnians , springtime means an uptick in respiratory conditions like hay fever and seasonal asthma .

Every day from October to December, Melbourne's pollen count is measured and published , so hay fever sufferers know exactly what they're breathing.

While current air monitoring can distinguish grass pollen from other types, it can't identify which grass is producing it. This is because all grass pollen can look fairly similar under the microscope.

So in Melbourne, we don't know whether grass pollen comes from a single type of grass or many. We also don't know how that mix changes across the season, or from one year to the next.

But why does it matter so much to know exactly which grass is producing which pollen?

Because some grasses are far more allergenic than others, and knowing someone's pollen exposure can help allergists choose the best treatment.

On top of this, severe spring storms can trigger thunderstorm asthma events , which hit Melbourne on average once every seven years. Because these events are linked to ryegrass pollen, tracking when ryegrass is in the air helps flag periods of highest risk.

In 2016, Melbourne experienced the world's largest epidemic thunderstorm asthma event , resulting in more than 3,500 emergency department presentations, a 672% increase in respiratory hospital admissions and 10 deaths.

To get a clearer picture of the pollen in Melbourne's air, our team used DNA metabarcoding to identify what was in weekly air samples collected over two consecutive years.

DNA metabarcoding is a method for identifying all the species that have left traces of genetic material, known as environmental DNA, in a sample, whether that's seawater, soil or, in our case, air.

The technique relies on short, unique sequences, called barcodes, found in the genetic material of every plant and animal—much like scanning a barcode at the supermarket to find out what a product is.

Pull these barcodes from an environmental sample, match them against a huge library of known DNA sequences and you can identify the...
body.zh: 本文已根据 Science X 的编辑流程和政策进行审阅。编辑在确保内容可信度的同时强调了以下属性： 当大多数澳大利亚人说“空气中弥漫着春天的气息”时，他们是在比喻，因为白天变得越来越长，越来越温暖。 春天是一年中墨尔本空气中充满植物开花花粉的季节。 虽然这些含苞待放的花朵给许多人带来了欢乐，但对于大约五分之一的墨尔本人来说，春天意味着花粉热和季节性哮喘等呼吸道疾病的增加。 从 10 月到 12 月，每天都会测量并公布墨尔本的花粉数量，以便花粉热患者确切地知道他们呼吸的是什么。 虽然当前的空气监测可以区分草花粉和其他类型的花粉，但无法确定是哪种草产生的花粉。这是因为所有草花粉在显微镜下看起来都非常相似。 所以在墨尔本，我们不知道草花粉是来自单一类型的草还是来自多种类型的草。我们也不知道这种组合在整个赛季或从一年到下一年之间如何变化。 但为什么准确了解哪种草产生哪种花粉如此重要呢？ 因为有些草比其他草更容易引起过敏，了解某人的花粉暴露情况可以帮助过敏症专家选择最佳治疗方法。 除此之外，严重的春季暴风雨可能引发雷暴哮喘事件，平均每七年袭击墨尔本一次。由于这些事件与黑麦草花粉有关，因此跟踪黑麦草何时出现在空气中有助于标记风险最高的时​​期。 2016年，墨尔本经历了全球最大规模的流行性雷暴哮喘事件，导致3500多人次急诊就诊，呼吸系统住院人数增加672%，死亡人数10人。 为了更清楚地了解墨尔本空气中的花粉，我们的团队使用 DNA 元条形码来识别连续两年收集的每周空气样本中的成分。 DNA 元条形码是一种识别样本中留下遗传物质（称为环境 DNA）痕迹的所有物种的方法，无论样本是海水、土壤还是空气。 该技术依赖于每种植物和动物的遗传物质中都存在的短而独特的序列（称为条形码），就像在超市扫描条形码来找出产品是什么一样。 通过 Phys.org 获取每日见解的超过 100,000 名订阅者发现科学、技术和太空领域的最新动态。订阅我们的免费时事通讯，每天或每周获取重要突破、创新和研究的最新动态。 从环境样本中提取这些条形码，将它们与已知 DNA 序列的巨大库进行匹配，您就可以识别...

reflection.en: As Melbourne awakens to spring, the air fills with pollen, bringing discomfort to many through hay fever and asthma. This seasonal challenge reminds us of our bodies' sensitivities and the ongoing need for healing and relief. We pray for those who suffer, asking for comfort and restoration from the ailments that mark this time of year.
reflection.zh: 随着墨尔本迎来春天，空气中弥漫着花粉，给许多人带来了过敏性鼻炎和哮喘的困扰。这个季节性的挑战提醒我们身体的敏感性，以及对治愈和缓解的持续需求。我们为那些受苦的人祈祷，祈求他们能从这一年一度的病痛中得到安慰和恢复。

verse.textEn: He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds.
verse.textZh: 他医好伤心的人，裹好他们的伤处。

title.en: Climate crisis probably weakened glacier that caused devastating Nepal-Tibet floods, first study finds
title.zh: 气候危机可能是导致尼泊尔-西藏洪水灾难的罪魁祸首，首次研究发现，此次洪水已造成1300多人死亡

summary.en: Scientists suggest that global heating destabilized a 200,000 sq meter glacier, leading to its collapse in August. This event triggered massive flash floods in Nepal and Tibet, causing over 1,300 deaths, according to the first scientific study of the disaster. The study noted unusually warm conditions preceding the...
summary.zh: 科学家们认为，全球变暖破坏了8月份倒塌的20万平方米的冰川。据首次对该灾难进行的科学研究显示，这一事件引发了尼泊尔和西藏大规模的洪水，造成1300多人死亡。研究指出，冰川倒塌前出现了异常的温暖天气，释放了1.1亿立方米的冰雪。

body.en: Scientists say global heating was a destabilising factor in collapse of 200,000 sq metre glacier in August Climate breakdown probably weakened the glacier that collapsed causing catastrophic floods and killing hundreds of people in Nepal and Tibet last month, the first scientific study of the disaster has found. Researchers identified unusually warm conditions before the glacier’s collapse , which sent an avalanche of 110m cubic metres (3,885 cu ft) of snow and ice into the valley below. This triggered flash floods on an almost unprecedented scale, hitting communities downstream without warning. Continue reading...
body.zh: 科学家表示，全球变暖是导致 8 月份 20 万平方米冰川崩塌的不稳定因素。第一项针对这场灾难的科学研究发现，气候崩溃可能削弱了上个月崩塌的冰川，导致尼泊尔和西藏发生灾难性洪水，造成数百人死亡。研究人员在冰川崩塌之前发现了异常温暖的气候，导致 110m 立方米（3,885 立方英尺）的雪和冰雪崩进入下面的山谷。这引发了几乎前所未有的规模的山洪，毫无预警地袭击了下游社区。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The earth itself groans, bearing the weight of human impact. This devastating flood, linked to climate breakdown, serves as a stark reminder of our interconnectedness with creation. As we witness such events, we are called to lament the damage and seek ways to live in greater harmony with the natural world Yahweh has entrusted to us.
reflection.zh: 大地本身也在呻吟，承受着人类活动带来的重负。这场与气候崩溃有关的毁灭性洪水，是提醒我们与雅伟所造之物息息相关的一个严峻教训。当我们目睹这样的事件时，我们被呼召为所造成的破坏而哀恸，并寻求以更和谐的方式与雅伟托付给我们的自然世界共处。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: Top Trump military adviser says US must prepare to fight around moon
title.zh: 特朗普高级军事顾问称美军须准备绕月作战

summary.en: General Dan Caine, Donald Trump's top military adviser, stated that US troops must prepare for combat not only in Earth's orbit but also around the moon. This comes after the US revealed it has deployed weapons in space, highlighting a new frontier in warfare.
summary.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普的首席军事顾问丹·凯恩将军表示，美军不仅要在地球轨道上，还必须准备在月球周围作战。此前，美国透露已在太空部署了武器，这标志着战争进入了一个新领域。

body.en: Gen Dan Caine comments at Washington summit come after US revealed it has deployed weapons in space American troops need to prepare for combat not only in Earth’s orbit but around the moon, Donald Trump’s top military adviser said on Wednesday, looking ahead to a new frontier in warfare after the US revealed for the first time that it has deployed weapons in space. Gen Dan Caine, chairman of the joint chiefs of staff, told service members and industry figures at the Air, Space and Cyber Conference outside Washington that the US military should adapt now so it “is prepared to fight, endure and win ... from the seabed to cislunar space”. Continue reading...
body.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普的高级军事顾问周三表示，在美国透露已在太空部署武器后，丹·凯恩将军在华盛顿峰会上发表评论，美国军队不仅需要为地球轨道和月球周围的战斗做好准备，在美国首次透露已在太空部署武器后，他展望了战争的新领域。参谋长联席会议主席丹·凯恩将军在华盛顿郊外举行的航空、航天和网络会议上对军人和业界人士表示，美国军队现在就应该做出调整，以便“做好战斗、忍受和胜利的准备……从海底到地月空间”。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The heavens declare the glory of Yahweh, yet humanity increasingly turns them into battlegrounds. As the US military prepares for conflict in cislunar space, we are reminded that the vastness above is not merely a strategic frontier, but a testament to the Creator's majesty. May we seek peace, not dominion, in all realms, terrestrial and celestial.
reflection.zh: 诸天述说雅伟的荣耀，但人类却日益将它们变成战场。当美军准备在地球月球空间（cislunar space）进行冲突时，我们被提醒，头顶的浩瀚之处不仅仅是战略前沿，更是造物主威严的见证。愿我们在地上和天上的所有领域都寻求和平，而非统治。

verse.textEn: The heavens declare the glory of God; the skies proclaim the work of his hands.
verse.textZh: 诸天述说神的荣耀，穹苍传扬他的手段。

title.en: Women with same health conditions as men ‘less likely to be offered active treatment’
title.zh: 患有与男性相同疾病的女性“不太可能接受积极治疗”

summary.en: A global analysis reveals that women with conditions like heart, kidney, or liver issues are less likely than men to receive interventions such as surgery, stents, or strong painkillers, indicating significant inequality in healthcare.
summary.zh: 一项全球分析显示，患有心脏、肾脏或肝脏疾病的女性，接受手术、支架或强效止痛药等治疗的可能性低于男性，这表明医疗保健方面存在显著的不平等。

body.en: Men with heart, kidney or liver conditions more likely to be offered intervention compared with women, global analysis finds Women with the same medical condition as men are less likely to be offered treatment such as surgery, a stent or a strong painkiller, research has found. A review of global research found that for several health problems, including cardiovascular conditions, kidney disease and Parkinson’s, women were less likely to receive the same treatment as men, revealing the extent to which women have significantly unequal care. Continue reading...
body.zh: 研究发现，与女性相比，患有心脏、肾脏或肝脏疾病的男性更有可能接受干预，研究发现，与男性健康状况相同的女性接受手术、支架或强效止痛药等治疗的可能性较小。一项对全球研究的回顾发现，对于包括心血管疾病、肾脏疾病和帕金森氏症在内的多种健康问题，女性接受与男性相同治疗的可能性较小，这揭示了女性所享受的护理存在明显不平等的程度。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This research points to a systemic disparity where women's health needs are not being met with the same urgency or intervention as men's. It calls for a voice to be raised on behalf of those who are overlooked, ensuring equitable care and treatment for all, regardless of gender.
reflection.zh: 这项研究指出了系统性的差异，女性的健康需求没有得到与男性同等的关注和干预。这呼吁为那些被忽视的群体发出声音，确保所有人都获得公平的医疗和治疗，无论其性别如何。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: Part-human part-mouse brain developed in science breakthrough
title.zh: 科学家开发出部分人类、部分小鼠的大脑

summary.en: Researchers at Stanford University have genetically modified mice to accept and function with human brain cells, aiming to test treatments for human-specific neurological and psychiatric diseases.
summary.zh: 斯坦福大学的研究人员对小鼠进行了基因改造，使其能够接受并与人类脑细胞协同工作，旨在测试人类特有的神经和精神疾病的治疗方法。

body.en:
Neuroscientists in the US have successfully adapted mice to have functioning human cells inside their own brains.

The researchers hope that potential treatments for psychiatric and neurodevelopmental diseases that only occur in humans could now be tested on the laboratory rodents.

While mice with brains that are partly human might sound like a Kafkaesque experiment, the scientists said these are not "mice that think like humans".

The animals are genetically engineered - and surgically altered - so that some of their brain tissue is human.

The scientists said their work, published in the journal Nature , external , was carried out with independent ethical scrutiny.

The aim of this ethically complicated breakthrough was to better understand the biology of brain disorders for which there are currently no effective treatments.

Some conditions cannot be studied in a mouse, simply because rodents do not develop some of the brain disorders that we do.

As lead researcher Prof Sergiu Pașca from Stanford University explained in a press conference, psychiatry has "one of the lowest success rates for clinical trials".

"Even drugs that actually make it to clinical trial - that seem to be working really well in animal models - fail dramatically in clinic," he said in a press conference. "That tells us we're missing a lot of information about human biology and capturing that will be essential."

The Stanford researchers said that, for some complex conditions, including epilepsy, autism and cerebral palsy, it has the potential to be "transformative".

Pașca said: "Here we have a new model that allows us to actually capture aspects of human brain function in a way that has not been possible before."

The human brain is made up of billions of cells, interconnected in millions of circuits, making it difficult to understand its development and what exactly is happening – at the cellular level - when things go wrong.

While this research is not the first time human neurons have been implanted in laboratory rodents , external , these scientists took that approach to a new level.

First, they genetically-engineered mice to develop almost none of their own cerebral cortex – that is the outer layer of the brain sometimes referred to as "grey matter". It handles higher-level thinking, memory and senses.

The researchers then used skin cells taken from humans and "reprogrammed" them, so they grew into pieces of brain-like tissue.

These are structures called organoids – they are not whole brains grown in dishes, more collections of connected, living cells.

When these organoids were implanted into the mouse brain the cells divided and organised themselves into the animal's existing brain circuitry, connecting with the rest of the mouse's brain and spinal cord.

The...
body.zh: 美国的神经科学家已经成功地让老鼠的大脑中拥有了具有功能的人类细胞。 研究人员希望，针对仅发生在人类身上的精神和神经发育疾病的潜在治疗方法现在可以在实验室啮齿动物身上进行测试。 虽然具有部分人类大脑的老鼠听起来像是卡夫卡式的实验，但科学家们表示，这些老鼠并不是“像人类一样思考的老鼠”。 这些动物经过基因工程改造，并通过手术改变，因此它们的一些脑组织是人类的。 科学家们表示，他们的工作发表在《自然》杂志上，外部，是在独立的道德审查下进行的。 这一伦理上复杂的突破的目的是更好地了解目前尚无有效治疗方法的脑部疾病的生物学原理。 有些病症无法在小鼠身上进行研究，因为啮齿类动物不会出现我们所患的某些大脑疾病。 正如斯坦福大学首席研究员 Sergiu Paşca 教授在新闻发布会上解释的那样，精神病学是“临床试验成功率最低的领域之一”。 他在新闻发布会上说：“即使是真正进入临床试验的药物——在动物模型中似乎效果很好——但在临床上却急剧失败。” “这告诉我们，我们错过了很多有关人类生物学的信息，捕捉这些信息至关重要。” 斯坦福大学的研究人员表示，对于一些复杂的疾病，包括癫痫、自闭症和脑瘫，它有可能具有“变革性”。 帕斯卡说：“我们有了一个新模型，它使我们能够以一种以前不可能的方式真正捕捉人类大脑功能的各个方面。” 人脑由数十亿个细胞组成，通过数百万个电路相互连接，因此很难理解其发育以及当出现问题时在细胞水平上到底发生了什么。 虽然这项研究并不是第一次将人类神经元植入实验室啮齿动物体内，但这些科学家将这种方法提升到了一个新的水平。 首先，他们对小鼠进行基因改造，使其几乎不发育出自己的大脑皮层——即大脑的外层，有时被称为“灰质”。它处理更高层次的思维、记忆和感官。 然后，研究人员使用取自人类的皮肤细胞并对它们进行“重新编程”，使它们长成类似大脑的组织碎片。 这些结构被称为类器官——它们不是在培养皿中生长的整个大脑，而是更多相连的活细胞的集合。 当这些类器官被植入小鼠大脑时，细胞分裂并组织成动物现有的大脑回路，与小鼠大脑和脊髓的其余部分连接。 这...

reflection.en: The creation of a mouse with human brain cells is a remarkable feat of scientific inquiry, echoing the ancient wisdom that creation itself reveals the Creator's works. As we explore the intricate machinery of life, may we do so with humility and awe, recognizing the profound intelligence woven into every living thing. This breakthrough, while raising...
reflection.zh: 创造出拥有人类脑细胞的小鼠是科学探索的非凡成就，它呼应了古老的智慧——创造本身揭示了造物主的作为。当我们探索生命的精密机制时，愿我们怀着谦卑和敬畏之心，认识到编织在万物中的深刻智慧。这项突破虽然引发了伦理问题，但也指出了通过仔细观察雅伟的创造所能学到的广阔知识。

verse.textEn: But ask the animals, and they will teach you, or the birds in the sky, and they will tell you; or speak to the earth, and it will teach you, or let the fish in the sea inform you.
verse.textZh: 你且问走兽，走兽必指教你；又问空中的飞鸟，飞鸟必告诉你。或与地说话，地必指教你；海中的鱼也必向你说明。

title.en: Scientists create mice with part-human brains
title.zh: 科学家创造部分人脑小鼠

summary.en: Researchers have engineered mice with partially human brains, transplanting lab-grown human brain cells into animals lacking a cortex or hippocampus. The goal is to better understand and treat neurological conditions like schizophrenia, epilepsy, cerebral palsy, intellectual disability, and rare dementias.
summary.zh: 研究人员通过将实验室培育的人脑细胞移植到缺乏皮层或海马体的小鼠体内，创造出了部分拥有人脑的小鼠。此举旨在更好地理解和治疗精神分裂症、癫痫、脑瘫、智力障碍以及罕见痴呆症等神经系统疾病。

body.en: Researchers hope to shed light on conditions such as schizophrenia, epilepsy, cerebral palsy, intellectual disability and rare forms of dementia Researchers have created mice with half-human brains in an effort to understand and develop new treatments for disorders such as schizophrenia, epilepsy, cerebral palsy, intellectual disability and rare forms of dementia. The scientists transplanted lab-grown human brain cells into animals that were engineered to be born without a cortex or hippocampus. This made space for the human tissue to grow inside the rodents’ skulls. Continue reading...
body.zh: 研究人员希望阐明精神分裂症、癫痫、脑瘫、智力障碍和罕见痴呆症等疾病。研究人员创造了具有半人脑的小鼠，以期了解和开发治疗精神分裂症、癫痫、脑瘫、智力障碍和罕见痴呆症等疾病的新疗法。科学家们将实验室培养的人类脑细胞移植到经过基因改造后没有皮质或海马体的动物体内。这为人体组织在啮齿类动物的头骨内生长提供了空间。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The creation of mice with part-human brains is a remarkable feat of scientific ingenuity. It prompts us to consider the intricate design of life, as Psalm 139:14 reminds us, 'I praise you because I am fearfully and wonderfully made.' This scientific endeavor, while seeking to alleviate suffering, also invites awe at the complexity of creation.
reflection.zh: 创造拥有部分人脑的小鼠是科学创造力的惊人壮举。这促使我们思考生命的精妙设计，正如诗篇139:14所提醒的：“我要称谢你，因我被造，奇妙可畏。”这项科学探索在寻求减轻痛苦的同时，也让我们对受造物的复杂性感到敬畏。

verse.textEn: I praise you because I am fearfully and wonderfully made; your works are wonderful, I know that full well.
verse.textZh: 我要称谢你，因我受造奇妙可畏；你的作为奇妙，这是我心深知道的。

title.en: Scientists turn seawater into fresh water without harmful brine
title.zh: 科学家将海水转化为淡水，无有害盐水

summary.en: Scientists have created a solar-powered desalination system that transforms seawater into fresh water, capturing nearly all the salt as a solid rather than producing harmful brine. This self-cleaning technology also has the potential to recover valuable minerals like lithium. Billions worldwide lack safe drinking...
summary.zh: 科学家开发了一种太阳能海水淡化系统，可将海水转化为淡水，并将几乎所有的盐分以固体形式去除，而不是产生有害的盐水。这项自清洁技术还有可能回收锂等有价值的矿物质。全球有数十亿人缺乏安全的饮用水，加利福尼亚和中东等地区日益依赖海水淡化，但目前的方法能耗高且可能带来环境问题。

body.en:
Around the world, billions of people still lack reliable access to safe drinking water. The United Nations estimates that 2.2 billion people do not have safely managed drinking water, while regions from California to the Middle East increasingly rely on desalination plants to turn ocean water into fresh water.

Desalination can provide a critical water supply, but today's most common methods come with significant drawbacks. Reverse osmosis forces water through specialized membranes to remove salt, while thermal distillation uses heat to separate fresh water from seawater. Both approaches can consume large amounts of energy, often require water treatment before and after the process, and generate a highly concentrated salty waste known as brine.

When that brine is discharged back into the ocean, it can increase local salinity and reduce oxygen levels, creating harmful conditions for marine organisms.

Researchers at the University of Rochester have developed a different approach that could help address several of those problems at once.

Scientists at URochester's Institute of Optics created a solar thermal desalination system designed to produce fresh water efficiently without generating liquid brine or requiring chemical additives to pre-treat the incoming water. The method is described in a paper published in Light: Science & Applications .

The research was led by Chunlei Guo, a professor of optics and physics and a senior scientist at URochester's Laboratory for Laser Energetics.

At the heart of the technology are solar panels made from black metal that has been treated with femtosecond lasers. A femtosecond is an extraordinarily short unit of time, equal to one quadrillionth of a second. Pulses from these ultrafast lasers can precisely alter a material's surface, creating microscopic structures that dramatically change how it interacts with light and water.

The laser treatment makes the metal extremely effective at absorbing sunlight and also gives it superwicking properties, meaning water spreads rapidly across the surface instead of beading up.

Each panel contains a laser-treated active region that draws a very thin layer of seawater across its surface. The dark metal absorbs nearly all of the incoming solar radiation, heating the water and causing it to evaporate.

That evaporation leaves salts and other dissolved minerals behind. Rather than allowing those materials to accumulate where evaporation is taking place, the panel directs them toward untreated areas along its sides, known as the passive region.

This movement is important because salt buildup is one of the biggest challenges facing solar desalination systems. If minerals form a hard layer across the active surface, they can block water movement and eventually stop the system...
body.zh: 在世界各地，数十亿人仍然无法获得可靠的安全饮用水。联合国估计，有 22 亿人没有安全管理的饮用水，而从加利福尼亚到中东的地区越来越依赖海水淡化厂将海水转化为淡水。 海水淡化可以提供关键的供水，但当今最常见的方法存在重大缺陷。反渗透迫使水通过专门的膜去除盐分，而热蒸馏则利用热量将淡水与海水分离。这两种方法都会消耗大量能源，通常需要在过程前后进行水处理，并产生高度浓缩的含盐废物，即盐水。 当盐水排回海洋时，它会增加当地的盐度并降低氧气含量，从而为海洋生物创造有害条件。 罗切斯特大学的研究人员开发了一种不同的方法，可以帮助同时解决其中几个问题。 罗彻斯特大学光学研究所的科学家们创建了一种太阳能热海水淡化系统，旨在高效生产淡水，无需产生液态盐水，也不需要化学添加剂来预处理进水。该方法在《光：科学与应用》上发表的一篇论文中进行了描述。 这项研究由光学和物理学教授、罗切斯特大学激光能量学实验室的高级科学家 Chunlei Guo 领导。 该技术的核心是由经过飞秒激光处理的黑色金属制成的太阳能电池板。飞秒是一个非常短的时间单位，等于万亿分之一秒。这些超快激光器发出的脉冲可以精确地改变材料的表面，形成微观结构，从而极大地改变材料与光和水相互作用的方式。 激光处理使金属能够非常有效地吸收阳光，并赋予其超吸湿特性，这意味着水会迅速扩散到表面，而不是形成水珠。 每个面板都包含一个经过激光处理的活性区域，该区域在其表面上绘制了一层非常薄的海水。深色金属吸收几乎所有入射的太阳辐射，加热水并导致其蒸发。 蒸发留下了盐和其他溶解的矿物质。面板不会让这些材料在发生蒸发的地方积聚，而是将它们引导到其两侧未经处理的区域，即所谓的被动区域。 这一运动很重要，因为盐积聚是太阳能海水淡化系统面临的最大挑战之一。如果矿物质在活性表面形成坚硬的层，它们会阻止水的运动并最终停止系统......

reflection.en: Human ingenuity, guided by observation of creation, can bring forth solutions to pressing global needs. The development of this solar-powered desalination system, turning a challenge into an opportunity to recover resources, reflects a deep engagement with the world Yahweh has made. It is a testament to the wisdom that can be found when we seek to...
reflection.zh: 人类的智慧，在对受造界的观察指引下，可以为紧迫的全球需求带来解决方案。这项太阳能海水淡化系统的开发，将挑战转化为回收资源的机遇，体现了对雅伟所造世界的深刻认识。它证明了当我们寻求理解并遵循自然界所蕴含的原则时，可以找到智慧。

verse.textEn: But ask the animals, and they will teach you, or the birds in the sky, and they will tell you; or speak to the earth, and it will teach you, or let the fish in the sea inform you.
verse.textZh: 你且问走兽，走兽必指教你；又问空中的飞鸟，飞鸟必告诉你。或与地说话，地必指教你；海中的鱼也必向你说明。

title.en: Scientists find an immune “false alarm” that may drive rapid aging
title.zh: 科学家发现可能导致快速衰老的免疫“假警报”

summary.en: Scientists have identified that severe genetic disorders linked to rapid aging might be caused by the body's overreaction to damaged DNA, rather than just the damage itself. An immune sensor, cGAS, can mistake DNA fragments in the wrong cellular location for a threat, triggering chronic inflammation that harms healthy...
summary.zh: 科学家发现，与快速衰老相关的某些严重遗传性疾病可能并非仅仅由DNA损伤引起，而是由身体对损伤的过度反应所驱动。当受损的DNA片段泄漏到细胞的错误区域时，一种名为cGAS的免疫传感器会将其误认为威胁，从而引发慢性炎症，损害健康组织。

body.en:
New research suggests that an overactive immune sensor may play a major role in severe genetic disorders linked to rapid aging. By reducing the activity of this sensor, scientists were able to improve tissue health across several biological systems, challenging long-held ideas about how DNA damage drives degeneration.

The immune system is designed to recognize and eliminate threats such as viruses. But under certain conditions, that protective machinery can mistakenly react to the body's own damaged DNA. When fragments of DNA are treated as if they came from an invading virus, the resulting immune response can trigger chronic inflammation that harms healthy tissue.

An international research team led by Dr. Marva Bergman and Prof. Itamar Harel at Hebrew University, working with Prof. Yehuda Tzfati, Prof. Ido Ben-Ami (Hebrew University and Sha'are Zedek Medical Center), and Prof. Bérénice Benayoun (University of Southern California), found that this misplaced immune reaction is a major contributor to tissue degeneration in severe, rapid-aging disorders.

When the researchers reduced this immune false alarm, they saw improvements across multiple biological systems.

The study focused on rare DNA damage-repair (DDR) syndromes such as Ataxia-Telangiectasia (A-T) and Bloom syndrome. In these disorders, the cellular systems responsible for repairing routine DNA damage do not work properly.

As a result, damaged DNA can accumulate throughout the body, creating genomic instability and contributing to neurodegeneration, increased cancer risk, and premature aging.

For decades, researchers largely assumed that the unrepaired DNA itself was the main force driving cellular decline. The new findings suggest the picture is more complicated.

"Our results show that the damage isn't acting alone," said Prof. Harel. "It's the body's response to that damage, an exaggerated, chronic inflammatory reaction, that drives much of the degeneration."

When DNA repair breaks down, pieces of DNA can escape into the cell's cytosol. Once there, they can activate a molecular sensor called cGAS.

Under normal circumstances, cGAS helps defend the body by detecting viral DNA. The problem is that the sensor cannot always distinguish foreign genetic material from fragments of the body's own DNA.

That confusion can lead to persistent sterile inflammation, meaning inflammation that occurs without an infection. Instead of protecting the body, the prolonged immune response begins damaging tissues.

In addition to activating inflammation, cGAS can move into the cell nucleus and directly disrupt DNA repair. That means the same molecule can contribute to degeneration in two ways: by promoting inflammation and by interfering with the cellular machinery that fixes damaged...
body.zh: 新的研究表明，过度活跃的免疫传感器可能在与快速衰老相关的严重遗传性疾病中发挥重要作用。通过减少这种传感器的活性，科学家们能够改善多个生物系统的组织健康，挑战了长期以来关于 DNA 损伤如何导致退化的观点。 免疫系统旨在识别和消除病毒等威胁。但在某些条件下，这种保护机制可能会错误地对人体自身受损的 DNA 做出反应。当 DNA 片段被视为来自入侵病毒时，产生的免疫反应可能引发慢性炎症，损害健康组织。 由希伯来大学 Marva Bergman 博士和 Itamar Harel 教授领导的国际研究小组与 Yehuda Tzfati 教授、Ido Ben-Ami 教授（希伯来大学和 Sha'are Zedek 医学中心）和 Bérénice Benayoun 教授（南加州大学）合作，发现这种错位的免疫反应是严重、快速衰老疾病中组织退化的主要原因。 当研究人员减少这种免疫误报时，他们看到了多个生物系统的改善。 该研究重点关注罕见的 DNA 损伤修复 (DDR) 综合征，例如共济失调毛细血管扩张症 (A-T) 和布卢姆综合征。在这些疾病中，负责修复常规 DNA 损伤的细胞系统无法正常工作。 因此，受损的 DNA 会在全身累积，造成基因组不稳定，导致神经退行性变、癌症风险增加和过早衰老。 几十年来，研究人员基本上认为未修复的 DNA 本身是驱动细胞衰退的主要力量。新的发现表明情况更加复杂。 哈雷尔教授说：“我们的研究结果表明，这种损害并不是单独发生的。” “正是身体对这种损害的反应，一种夸张的慢性炎症反应，导致了大部分退化。” 当 DNA 修复被破坏时，DNA 片段就会逃逸到细胞的细胞质中。一旦到达那里，他们就可以激活一种名为 cGAS 的分子传感器。 正常情况下，cGAS 通过检测病毒 DNA 来帮助保护身体。问题是传感器不能总是区分外来遗传物质和人体自身 DNA 片段。 这种混淆可能会导致持续性无菌性炎症，即在没有感染的情况下发生的炎症。长时间的免疫反应不但没有保护身体，反而开始损害组织。 除了激活炎症外，cGAS 还可以进入细胞核并直接破坏 DNA 修复。这意味着同一个分子可以通过两种方式导致退化：促进炎症和干扰修复受损细胞的细胞机制......

reflection.en: The intricate workings of the human body, even its defense mechanisms, reveal profound complexity. This research into the immune system's 'false alarms' highlights how much we can learn about life's processes through careful observation and study, echoing the ancient wisdom that creation itself speaks of its Maker's design.
reflection.zh: 人体复杂的运作机制，甚至是其防御机制，都揭示了深刻的奥秘。这项关于免疫系统“假警报”的研究表明，通过细致的观察和学习，我们可以从生命的过程中获得多少知识，这呼应了古老的智慧——受造界本身就诉说着造物主的智慧与设计。

title.en: Wildlife trust wants marina silt disposed offshore
title.zh: 野生动物信托基金希望将码头淤泥运往近海处理

summary.en: Brighton Marina plans to resume dredging next year but requires a location for the removed silt. A wildlife trust is advocating for an offshore disposal site, expressing concern over proposed plans near Newhaven, which is adjacent to a protected marine conservation zone.
summary.zh: 布莱顿码头计划明年恢复疏浚作业，但需要一个淤泥处理地点。一个野生动物信托基金呼吁在近海设立淤泥处理点，并对在新港附近进行的计划表示担忧，该区域毗邻一个受保护的海洋保护区。

body.en:
A wildlife trust has called for a new offshore disposal site to be found for sediment dredged from Brighton Marina, saying it remains concerned about plans being explored off Newhaven.

Brighton Marina has been looking for a long-term disposal site since Sussex Wildlife Trust successfully challenged a licence in 2025 for disposal of sediment at Rottingdean.

The marina has said dredging is needed to maintain safe access and there are limited options available for disposal sites.

Sussex Wildlife Trust said Newhaven was a "protected area" that sat adjacent to the Beachy Head West Marine Conservation Zone (MCZ).

Campaigners previously claimed the silt was a " black, thick, slimy, petrochemically smelling sludge ", but Premier Marinas, which owns Brighton Marina, said dredged silt was regularly sampled to confirm it was not harmful.

John Cervenka, Premier Marinas chief operating officer, said: "Maintaining safe navigational access to Brighton Marina is not optional. It is a legal requirement and fundamental to the operation of the marina."

According to the marina, about 150 businesses depend on the site, creating jobs for about 1,200 people, with more than eight million visits each year.

Premier Marinas said Newhaven had been identified as a potential alternative by Sussex Wildlife Trust.

However, the trust said in a statement on social media , external : "We have not promoted or endorsed Newhaven over any other option."

The trust said: "Newhaven sits adjacent to Beachy Head West MCZ, and we remain concerned about potential impacts on this protected area.

The trust said that Newhaven was already used for dredge disposal by Newhaven Port, and there was currently no available data on the impacts of additional disposal there.

Until it saw further evidence, it did not have a view on whether Newhaven was suitable, it added.

"We will respond to any future licence application based on the ecological evidence it contains," it said.

Brighton Marina hopes to submit a marine licence application to the Marine Management Organisation in November.

Follow BBC Sussex on Facebook , external , X , external , and Instagram , external and listen to BBC Radio Sussex on Sounds . Send your story ideas to southeasttoday@bbc.co.uk , external or WhatsApp us on 08081 002250.
body.zh: 一个野生动物信托基金呼吁为从布莱顿码头挖出的沉积物找到一个新的海上处置场，并表示仍然对纽黑文附近正在探索的计划感到担忧。 自苏塞克斯野生动物信托基金于 2025 年成功挑战罗廷丁沉积物处置许可证以来，布莱顿码头一直在寻找长期处置场。 码头表示，需要进行疏浚以保持安全通道，并且可供处置场所的选择有限。 苏塞克斯野生动物信托基金表示，纽黑文是一个“保护区”，毗邻比奇角西海洋保护区（MCZ）。 活动人士此前声称这些淤泥是“黑色、粘稠、粘稠、有石化气味的污泥”，但布莱顿码头的所有者Premier Marinas表示，定期对疏浚的淤泥进行取样，以确认其无害。 Premier Marinas 首席运营官 John Cervenka 表示：“维持布莱顿码头的安全航行通道不是可选的。这是一项法律要求，也是码头运营的基础。” 据码头称，约有 150 家企业依赖该码头，为约 1,200 人创造了就业机会，每年接待游客量超过 800 万人次。 总理马里纳斯表示，苏塞克斯野生动物信托基金已将纽黑文确定为潜在的替代方案。 然而，该信托基金在社交媒体外部的一份声明中表示：“我们没有提倡或认可纽黑文而不是任何其他选择。” 该信托基金表示：“纽黑文毗邻 Beachy Head West MCZ，我们仍然担心对该保护区的潜在影响。 该信托机构表示，纽黑文港已使用纽黑文进行挖泥船处置，目前没有关于额外处置影响的可用数据。 它补充说，在看到进一步的证据之前，它对纽黑文是否合适没有看法。 “我们将根据其中包含的生态证据对未来的任何许可证申请做出回应，”它说。 布莱顿码头希望在11月份向海洋管理组织提交海洋许可证申请。 在 Facebook、external、X、external 和 Instagram、external 上关注 BBC Sussex，并在 Sounds 上收听 BBC Radio Sussex。将您的故事想法发送至Southeasttoday@bbc.co.uk、外部或WhatsApp我们08081 002250。

reflection.en: The Sussex Wildlife Trust's plea highlights the intricate balance of ecosystems and the need for careful stewardship of marine environments. It reminds us that Yahweh's creation is filled with diverse life and wisdom, which we are called to protect and understand, not disrupt through expediency.
reflection.zh: 苏塞克斯野生动物信托基金的呼吁突显了生态系统的复杂平衡以及审慎管理海洋环境的必要性。这提醒我们，雅伟的创造充满了多样的生命和智慧，我们被呼召去保护和理解它，而不是出于便利而破坏它。

verse.textEn: How many are your works, Yahweh! In wisdom you made them all; the earth is full of your creatures.
verse.textZh: 雅伟啊，你所造的何其多！都是你用智慧造成的；遍地满了你的丰富。

title.en: Endangered water voles introduced to reserve
title.zh: 濒危水䶄被引入保护区

summary.en: Efforts are underway to reintroduce the locally extinct water vole species back to the River Wey in Surrey, with 30 nationally endangered water voles released into a nature reserve near Elstead.
summary.zh: 为重新引入已在当地灭绝的水䶄物种回到萨里郡的韦伊河，目前正进行着努力，已有30只全国濒危的水䶄被释放到埃尔斯特德附近的一个自然保护区。

body.en:
Surrey Wildlife Trust has introduced 30 nationally-endangered water voles to a nature reserve near Elstead.

The release on the River Wey comes following a "successful" release on the upper river.

The water voles are being introduced downstream on 10 sites between Frensham and Elstead, the wildlife trust said.

James Herd, director of reserves management at the trust, said: "As we work towards the restoration of natural ecosystems and landscapes county wide, I hope this release is one of many reintroductions of native species that we'll see in the years ahead."

Water voles have been functionally extinct in Surrey since the early 2000s, but co-ordinated reintroduction and habitat improvement efforts by nature restoration groups are working to help the endearing species thrive again.

The trust said in a statement that it hoped that over the coming months, the aquatic rodents will "adapt easily to life on the 16-hectare reserve at Thundry Meadows and establish widely across the top of the Wey catchment".

Their return would also benefit other species which depend on healthy wetland habitats including herons and birds of prey, they added.

David Elliott, National Trust lead ranger for the South Downs West said: "Nature wins when we work together."

"It's so encouraging to see the water voles returning after all this time, they have been locally extinct for decades.

The release is part of a wider effort led by the National Trust, River Wey Trust and South East Rivers Trust to reintroduce the locally extinct species back to the River Wey.

body.zh: 萨里野生动物信托基金已将 30 只国家濒临灭绝的水田鼠引入埃尔斯特德附近的自然保护区。 继上游河流“成功”放生之后，威河上又放生了。 野生动物基金会表示，水田鼠正在从弗伦舍姆和埃尔斯特德之间的 10 个地点引入下游。 该信托基金保护区管理总监詹姆斯·赫德 (James Herd) 表示：“在我们努力恢复全县自然生态系统和景观的过程中，我希望此次放归是我们在未来几年将看到的众多本地物种重新引入之一。” 自 2000 年代初以来，萨里的水田鼠已经功能性灭绝，但自然恢复团体协调重新引入和栖息地改善工作正在努力帮助这一可爱的物种再次繁衍生息。 该信托基金在一份声明中表示，希望在未来几个月内，这些水生啮齿动物能够“轻松适应 Thundry Meadows 16 公顷保护区的生活，并在 Wey 流域顶部广泛定居”。 他们补充说，它们的回归也将使依赖健康湿地栖息地的其他物种受益，包括苍鹭和猛禽。 国家信托基金 (National Trust) 南部唐斯西区 (South Downs West) 首席护林员大卫·埃利奥特 (David Elliott) 表示：“当我们共同努力时，自然就会获胜。” “看到水田鼠在这么久之后又回来了，真是令人鼓舞，它们在当地已经灭绝了几十年。 这次释放是国家信托基金、韦伊河信托基金和东南河流信托基金领导的更广泛努力的一部分，旨在将当地灭绝的物种重新引入韦伊河。 在 Facebook、external、X、external 和 Instagram、external 上关注 BBC Surrey，并收听 BBC Radio Surrey 的 Sounds。将您的故事想法发送至Southeasttoday@bbc.co.uk、外部或WhatsApp我们08081 002250。

reflection.en: The successful reintroduction of 30 endangered water voles to the River Wey is a hopeful sign of ecological restoration. It reminds us of the inherent goodness of creation, as described in Genesis 1:31, and the importance of human stewardship in preserving it for future generations.

body.en:
The head of Microsoft AI has warned that without adequate safeguards, the development of AI could lead to the emergence of a new "silicon species" wich competes with humans.

Mustafa Suleyman said rival firm Anthropic is treating AI like it is human, an approach he called "misguided" which could create technology that humanity cannot control.

Speaking to the BBC's Today programme, the chief executive said it was "right" for people to be concerned about AI, but there were "very practical things that we can do" to control it.

The comments are the latest in a series of stark warnings from the AI industry about the technology's possible dangers. Anthropic has been approached for comment.

Speaking to the Today programme on Thursday, Suleyman warned against firms continuing to create AI systems capable of setting their own objectives, earning money and owning assets.

That would mean "essentially seeding a new silicon species", he said, which could "no doubt compete with us for resources, no matter how much it cares about humanity and loves us".

Suleyman's comments to the BBC follow an essay he published earlier this week , external , in which he questioned Anthropic's approach to training its AI model Claude, despite praising boss Dario Amodei and his team as "intellectually honest people".

In it, he criticised Anthropic for teaching its AI to have human-like qualities, a practice known as anthropomorphising, which he said made it seem as though Claude had its own desires, values and sense of self.

He also warned tech firms risk creating something "impossible" to control by treating the technology like a human.

"They do not feel, experience, or suffer. They do not have innate preferences or underlying motivations.

"They are sequence completion engines, internally hollow, designed to follow instructions, and accomplish goals set by humans."

The Microsoft boss said greater transparency was needed around how AI systems are trained and evaluated.

This, he said, included independent scrutiny of AI behaviour and stronger tools to monitor and control the technology.

"We must not sleepwalk our way into a decision we later come to bitterly regret," he wrote.

Dame Wendy Hall, professor of Computer Science at the University of Southampton, described the comments as "the sort of conversation we need to be having internationally", contrasting it with the "histrionics" from some AI companies which she said only served to "scare everyone".

The question of how much autonomy AI systems should have is increasingly dividing the industry.

Speaking to the BBC about an upcoming AI summit, Suleyman called for "alignment" to create technology that must be "subordinate" to humanity.
